title: Normalized descent of ordinary-etale shifted lines on an affine line
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $A$ a finite commutative ring, $a:X=\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ and $i_1:S\to X$ the section $t=1$. Work on small etale sites, with ordinary constant-$A$ module inverse images and unbounded derived categories. A locally constant free rank-one sheaf means a sheaf etale locally isomorphic to $A$. For every such sheaf $L$ on $S$, an automorphism $u:a^*L\to a^*L$ with $i_1^*u=1_L$ is the identity. This holds over arbitrary $S$, including empty or nonreduced schemes and for the zero ring $A$.
Let $m\in\mathbf Z$, let $C\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $F\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have $C[-m]$ and $F[-m]$ isomorphic to locally constant free rank-one sheaves, and let $\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ be specified. Suppose an etale cover $\{S_i\to S\}$ and isomorphisms $\lambda_i:F|_{X_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_i^*(C|_{S_i})$, $X_i=\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$, are given, with $i_1^*\lambda_i=\theta|_{S_i}$ under the inverse-image compositors. Then the $\lambda_i$ agree on every overlap, their inverses agree, and there is a unique isomorphism
$$\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C,\qquad i_1^*\kappa=\theta.$$
It restricts to each $\lambda_i$ and is independent of the chosen normalized local comparisons and cover. The uniqueness is among all normalized global isomorphisms, not just ones already known to restrict to the specified $\lambda_i$.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Gluing, comparison of ratios on geometric affine-line fibres and gluing maps and inverses; old item Steps 10–11.

proof.text: First prove the sheaf assertion, in fact for any sheaf $L$ of $A$-modules. By [new-lem-pur-etale-a1-pullback-full], the ordinary functor $a^*$ is full for this arbitrary scheme $S$ and commutative ring $A$. Hence there is a sheaf endomorphism $b:L\to L$ with $u=a^*b$. Applying $i_1^*$ and using the natural identification $i_1^*a^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ specified in the statement gives $b=i_1^*u=1_L$. Functoriality then gives $u=a^*(1_L)=1_{a^*L}$. Only fullness was used; no claim that $i_1^*$ is faithful on all sheaves on $X$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A3H, lemma-sections-upstairs, connected-fibre argument, in the existing affine-line fullness node; blueprint sk-thm-dnc.proof.md, Gluing, rigidity of the ratio

proof.text: Choose sheaves $P$ on $X$ and $Q$ on $S$ and isomorphisms $F[-m]\cong P[0]$, $C[-m]\cong Q[0]$, as the hypotheses allow. Fixed-coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Its termwise derived functor commutes with shifts and takes $Q[0]$ to $(a^*Q)[0]$ by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Shift every given map by $[-m]$ and conjugate with these fixed isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of the single-complex functor [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies the resulting maps, their compositions and their inverses with unique ordinary sheaf maps. Thus $\theta$ becomes an isomorphism $\vartheta:i_1^*P\to Q$ and $\lambda_i$ becomes an isomorphism $l_i:P|_{X_i}\to a_i^*(Q|_{S_i})$ normalized by $i_1^*l_i=\vartheta|_{S_i}$. These identifications commute with restriction: termwise inverse image of a single complex is the single complex of the inverse image, also on morphisms. The supplied inverse-image compositors are used throughout. Undoing the shift is an inverse equivalence, so all sheaf equalities proved below give precisely the required derived equalities.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts, part (2); Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; blueprint sk-thm-dnc.proof.md, opening paragraph: morphisms between these complexes are sheaf morphisms

proof.text: Put $S_{ij}=S_i\times_SS_j$ and $X_{ij}=X\times_SS_{ij}$. From the fibre-product definition of affine space [def-sbc-affine-space], $X\times_SS_i\cong\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$ and $X_{ij}\cong\mathbf A^1_{S_{ij}}$: an arrow into either side is exactly an arrow into the new base together with an arrow into $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t]$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The two descriptions therefore have the same projections and the same section $t=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], the $X_i\to X$ form an etale covering family, and pulling the $S_i\to S$ back to any $S_j$ again gives an etale cover. Consequently all the restrictions and overlaps used below are small-etale restrictions and the argument of Step 1 applies with base $S_{ij}$.

source.place: Gluing, base change to S_i times_S S_j

proof.text: On $X_{ij}$ write $l_i,l_j$ for the two restrictions, using the prescribed compositors, and form $r_{ij}=l_j\circ l_i^{-1}$, an automorphism of $a_{ij}^*(Q|_{S_{ij}})$. Normalization gives $i_1^*r_{ij}=\vartheta|_{S_{ij}}\circ(\vartheta|_{S_{ij}})^{-1}=1$. Step 1 over $S_{ij}$ gives $r_{ij}=1$, whence $l_j=r_{ij}l_i=l_i$. Their inverses agree too: multiply $l_j=l_i$ on the left by $l_j^{-1}$ and on the right by $l_i^{-1}$. These are equalities of sheaf maps, hence also of the original derived maps by Step 2.

source.place: Gluing, the two normalized local isomorphisms differ by an automorphism, which is the identity

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-etale-sheaf-hom-family-gluing] to the sheaves $P,a^*Q$, the covering family $X_i\to X$ of Step 3, and the maps $l_i$ of Step 4. Its compatibility condition on every etale object $W$ mapping to two cover members holds: the two arrows give an arrow $W\to X_{ij}$ by the fibre-product universal property, and restricting $l_i=l_j$ along it gives exactly the required equality with the canonical localization identifications. This yields a unique sheaf map $k:P\to a^*Q$ restricting to every $l_i$. Apply the same node to the inverse maps to obtain $h:a^*Q\to P$. Both $hk$ and $1_P$ restrict to $1_{P|_{X_i}}$, and both $kh$ and $1_{a^*Q}$ restrict to $1_{(a^*Q)|_{X_i}}$; the uniqueness clause of the gluing node gives $hk=1_P$ and $kh=1_{a^*Q}$. Thus $k$ is an isomorphism. Step 2 returns an isomorphism $\kappa:F\to a^*C$ with all the required restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03EM, lemma-internal-hom, via Sites Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; blueprint sk-thm-dnc.proof.md, Gluing, glue maps and inverses

proof.text: The sheaf maps $i_1^*k$ and $\vartheta$ on $S$ restrict to the same map on every $S_i$, since $k|_{X_i}=l_i$ and the latter were normalized. Uniqueness in [lem-amb-etale-sheaf-hom-family-gluing], now on the cover $S_i\to S$, gives $i_1^*k=\vartheta$, hence $i_1^*\kappa=\theta$. For any other normalized global isomorphism $\kappa'$, Step 2 turns its ratio $\kappa'\kappa^{-1}$ into a sheaf automorphism of $a^*Q$ whose restriction along $i_1$ is the identity. Step 1 gives that ratio equal to the identity, so $\kappa'=\kappa$ without assuming any local restriction for $\kappa'$. Any other normalized local comparison on any cover equals the restriction of $\kappa$ by the same ratio argument over its base. This proves independence of both comparisons and cover. If $S$ is empty, the gluing node explicitly allows its empty cover, and the same uniqueness statements apply. For $A=0$ all module sheaves are zero and the argument still applies; no step used a nonzero coefficient, reduced base, invertible exponent, or finite-type hypothesis.

source.place: Gluing, unique isomorphism normalized at t=1; explicit global uniqueness and degenerate cases
